title_ar: الشيخ الددو يختتم برنامجه الدعوي في الشرق الموريتاني من ولاية لعصابة
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Concludes His Da'wah Programme in Eastern Mauritania from the Region of Assaba
body_ar:
اختتم فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو البارحة ( ليلة الخميس ) 13 سبتمبر 2023م - بمقاطعة كرو برنامجه الدعوي بمحاضرة بعنوان: الأمانة ومسؤولية تحملها احتضنها مسجد مركز وادان بالمقاطعة
تحدث فيها عن الأمانة وما يترتب عليها من أحكام مبينا أن المسلمين عند عهودهم، وأن الله تعالى قال في كتابه "إنا عرضنا الأمانة على السموات والأرض والجبال فأبين أن يحملنها وأشفقن منها وحملها الإنسان إنه كان ظلوما جهولا"
مؤكدا أن من خصائص المسلم الوفاء بالعهود، وتحمل الأمانة؛ فهي عهد وميثاق، وقد حذر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من تضييعها، فلا خير في من يضيع أمانته.
وتأتي هذه المحاضرة ضمن رحلة دعوية نظمتها جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم تضمنت أكثر من عشر محاضرات ودروس احتضنتها كل من اغشوركيت وبوخزامة والنعمة وتنبدغة ولعيون والطينطان وكيفة وكرو تحدث فيهن عن واجبات المسلم تجاه دينه ومقدساته، وخصائص المجتمع المسلم، ومحبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، والأمانة ومسؤولية تحملها.
كما تضمنت دروسا لطلاب العلم حثهم فيها على بذل الجهد واستغلال فرص تحصيل العلوم، وإخلاص النية في ذلك لله.
وكان الشيخ الددو قد افتتح برنامجه لهذا اليوم بمحاضرة في مسجد المعهد العلمي بمقاطعة كيفة - عاصمة ولاية لعصابة - حذر فيها المسلمين من اتباع الشهوات فهي من الفتن الظاهرة التي تزيل النعم
كما دعاهم إلى التمسك بالسنة الغراء محذرا من خطر الديانة الإبراهيمية مؤكدا أنها غزو عالمي لإفساد عقيدة المسلمين لذلك جاءت قبلها دعوات ممهدة لها كالتشكيك في السنة والطعن في صحتها والترويج للأفكار الداعية إلى فصل القرآن عن السنة النبوية المطهرة.
body_en:
Yesterday (Wednesday night), 13 September 2023, in the district of Kouro, His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew concluded his da'wah programme with a lecture entitled "The Trust and the Responsibility of Bearing It", hosted by the mosque of the Wadan centre in the district.
In it he spoke about the trust (amānah) and the rulings that follow from it, explaining that the Muslims stand by their covenants, and that God Almighty said in His Book {We offered the trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they refused to bear it and were afraid of it, and man bore it — he is indeed given to wrongdoing and ignorant} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:72)
affirming that among the characteristics of the Muslim are the keeping of covenants and the bearing of the trust; for it is a covenant and a solemn pledge, and the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, warned against squandering it, so that there is no good in one who squanders his trust.
This lecture comes within a da'wah tour organised by the al-Mustaqbal Association for Da'wah, Culture and Education, which took in more than ten lectures and classes hosted by each of Aghchorguitt, Boukhzama, Néma, Timbedra, Aioun, Tintane, Kiffa and Kouro, in which he spoke about the Muslim's duties towards his religion and its sanctities, the characteristics of the Muslim society, love for the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace, and the trust and the responsibility of bearing it.
It also took in classes for students of knowledge, in which he urged them to exert themselves and to make use of the opportunities for acquiring the sciences, and to keep their intention in that sincere to God.
Sheikh al-Dedew had opened his programme for that day with a lecture at the mosque of the scholarly institute in the district of Kiffa — capital of the region of Assaba — in which he warned the Muslims against following the appetites, for they are among the manifest trials that take blessings away;
and he called on them to hold fast to the resplendent sunnah, warning of the danger of the Abrahamic religion and affirming that it is a global incursion aimed at corrupting the creed of the Muslims, and that for this reason there came before it calls that prepared the ground for it, such as casting doubt on the sunnah and impugning its soundness, and promoting the ideas that call for separating the Qur'an from the purified prophetic sunnah.

flags.context: what the report says the Sheikh warned against
flags.note: Not a reference to Abraham, and not the academic phrase 'the Abrahamic faiths'. In Arabic religious discourse of this period al-diyānah al-Ibrāhīmiyyah names a specific alleged project to merge Islam, Christianity and Judaism into one religion, associated by its critics with the Abraham Accords. A bare 'the Abrahamic religion' may read in English as a reference to interfaith dialogue in general, which is not what is meant. Flagged rather than glossed, because adding the explanation would be adding a claim the source does not make.

flags.context: the dateline of the lecture that closed the tour
options: Yesterday, the night before Thursday, 13 September 2023
flags.note: ليلة الخميس in Arabic usage is the night that precedes Thursday, i.e. Wednesday night, because the Islamic day begins at sunset. Rendering it 'Thursday night' would move the event a day. 13 September 2023 was in fact a Wednesday, which supports this reading. The source defect is not in the Arabic but in any naive English rendering of it.

translator_notes: A news report by the site's news desk. The summary of the lectures is the desk's, not the Sheikh's wording.
The Qur'anic quotation is given in curly quotation marks with its reference per style guide section 4. Qur'anic renderings in this corpus are interpretive and not a substitute for the Arabic.
الفتن الظاهرة is 'the manifest trials' — fitan, trials or temptations, not 'seditions' in this context.

Place names follow the Mauritanian official spellings. مسجد مركز وادان is given as 'the mosque of the Wadan centre'; Wadan here is the name of a local centre, not the historic town of Ouadane in Adrar.
editorial_review_reasons: The record reports the Sheikh warning against 'the Abrahamic religion' as a global incursion aimed at corrupting Muslim creed. In English, and detached from the specific interfaith-merger project the Arabic phrase names, this can be read as hostility to Jews and Christians as such, and as opposition to interfaith work generally. That misreading carries reputational exposure in Western jurisdictions. The passage has been translated faithfully and neither softened nor strengthened, and the ambiguity is recorded as a flag; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.
